title: Tenali Raman and the Secret of the Singing Fish

full_text:
A traveling showman named Mayadas set up a colorful tent on the banks of the Tungabhadra River, displaying a large glass tank containing an enormous silver river carp.
He proclaimed to the crowds:
'Behold the Miraculous Singing Fish of the Saraswati!
When I play my flute, this sacred fish surfaces, opens its mouth, and sings ancient hymns in a sweet, melodious soprano voice!'

Citizens paid silver coins to enter.
Mayadas played his flute, the silver carp swam to the glass, opened and closed its mouth in rhythm—and indeed, a clear, sweet soprano voice filled the tent, singing beautiful melodies!
The citizens were spellbound, dropping gold and silver into the charity bowl.
Even several ministers reported to King Krishnadevaraya that a celestial reincarnation had appeared in the river.

Tenali Raman visited the tent, accompanied by his young nephew.
Tenali watched the tank intently.
He noticed that the fish opened and closed its mouth naturally to breathe water through its gills, matching the tempo of the flute.
He also noticed that the water in the glass tank showed zero acoustic ripples or vibrations while the song was being sung!
A voice powerful enough to fill a large tent should create circular sound ripples upon the surface of still water!

Tenali walked around the tent.
Behind the display platform stood a large, ornate wooden wardrobe draped in heavy red velvet curtains, supposedly containing 'ceremonial water jugs'.
Tenali gently took out a small hollow reed blowpipe from his sash, loaded it with a tiny pinch of fine black pepper, and blew it through a small seam in the back of the velvet wardrobe!

Within ten seconds, a violent, desperate sneeze erupted from inside the wardrobe:
*‘ACHOOO! ACHO0-OOF! COUGH!’*
And the 'singing fish' in the tank was suddenly interrupted mid-verse by an unmistakable, very human cough coming from inside the furniture!

Tenali pulled aside the heavy velvet curtain and swung open the wardrobe door:
Crouched inside upon a stool, holding a polished brass acoustic speaking-tube that funneled sound directly beneath the fish tank, was Mayadas’s sixteen-year-old sister, wiping her streaming eyes and coughing from the pepper!

The crowd gasped in outrage at the exposed deception!
The showman fell to the floor, begging Tenali for mercy.
Tenali smiled:
'Fish swim and breathe, but they do not sing in soprano!
Whenever you hear an impossible voice coming from a creature that has no vocal cords, search behind the nearest velvet curtain!'

The showman was ordered to refund all coins to the citizens, and Tenali’s sharp observational logic was celebrated across Vijayanagara.
moral: Supernatural marvels that extract money from the public are exposed when their hidden acoustics are traced.
